title: The Concept of Quantum Entanglement
text:
Quantum entanglement describes a physical phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same quantum state. Regardless of the distance separating them, measuring the property of one particle instantaneously influences the corresponding property of the others, a correlation Einstein famously termed 'spooky action at a distance.'

This non-local connection suggests that physical reality may be more interconnected than classical physics models predict. Unlike correlations based on hidden variables, entanglement necessitates quantum mechanics itself for its description, making it a cornerstone concept in developing quantum computing and secure communication protocols.

Experimental verification of entanglement, often through Bell's inequalities, has continually confirmed the predictions of quantum theory, solidifying its role as one of modern physics' most profound mysteries and greatest technological potentials.
